analysis: Integrated 13 units across docs (changelog.d/coordinator-traffic-verdict.md, docs/provider/cli-reference.md Traffic bullet ~1045-1062, docs/provider/troubleshooting.md lines 83 and 143), Swift diagnostics/recovery (ServingReadiness.swift verdict refactor with new .unconfirmed and routed-request path, UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.swift removal of connectionLacksAuthorization, ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift noteCoordinatorRequest and verdict-based supervision, ProviderLoop+Serve.swift lines 429-432, ProviderLoop+Trust.swift receivedAt default, DaemonStateFile.swift optional lastRequestAt, DoctorRunner/StatusCommand+Traffic rendering, ProviderLogger fixed-vocabulary message) and tests. The changes are local diagnostic and re-registration pacing logic. Nothing observed grants serving authorization: the coordinator stays authoritative (A-016, TB-011, T-052/T-053). A routed request is recorded only from coordinator-sent .inferenceRequest events on the authenticated TB-002 socket; it cannot be forged locally, and tests show untrusted status and an expired lease still block. Request and decryption paths in Serve.swift are unchanged, so there is no new plaintext exposure. lastRequestAt is a timestamp only in an existing diagnostic state file, a minor metadata exposure that does not qualify as a finding (T-058). The log message is a closed enum, so the public-log contract is preserved. Availability effect (T-057/A-018): stale refusals now read unconfirmed and do not trigger re-registration, so recovery could be suppressed if the coordinator stops repeating a refusal. This is a documented design choice, with idle gating, jitter and backoff retained. Unverified, since the sources were not supplied or were truncated: the full ServingReadiness.verdict logic (ordering of lastRequestAt versus trust.receivedAt, and that unconfirmed or pending never upgrade authorization), the callers of handleTrustStatus(receivedAt:) to confirm the timestamp is never coordinator-controlled, and logSinkForTesting not being reachable in release builds. Integration replay covered only docs, so Swift conclusions rest on the prior unit analyses. No concrete regression is identified; a deeper pass on ServingReadiness.swift and its supervisor callers is advised.
